🌾 When did your village peak? France, 1793 → 2021

Every French commune, coloured against its own population record: gold while it is at its all-time high, blue once it has fallen below it. Around 1800 the whole map glows — most French people still lived in villages. Then industry and the railways drew people into the towns, and the countryside went dark: by 1950, 9 communes in 10 had at least 10% fewer people than at their peak, and 7 in 10 had peaked before 1900. After 1960 the light returns, but only around cities, suburbs and the coasts 🏙️

📊 Data: French Historical GIS (Litvine, Séguy, Thévenin et al., CC BY-NC 4.0), commune censuses 1793–1999 at the borders of each date; Eurostat Census 2021 1 km grid for 2021. The counter covers the 34,018 communes with a complete series and stops at the last commune census (1999).
